topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture objectives, historical context, and framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and proliferative signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt/beta-catenin pathways drive self-sufficient proliferation and survival signaling.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how disruptions in normal cellular differentiation pathways maintain cells in proliferative states across leukemias and colorectal carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells resist programmed cell death by altering the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins in the p53 pathway.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomere maintenance, and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms of telomere shortening, senescence induction, and telomerase reactivation that enable cancer cells to achieve unlimited replicative potential.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe cancer-associated metabolic rewiring, including aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations that generate epigenetic oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how growing tumors overcome diffusion limits by shifting the angiogenic balance to stimulate new blood vessel formation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and dynamics of invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step metastatic cascade, circulating tumor cell monitoring, seed-and-soil interactions, and metastatic genomic alterations.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks and reflections on evolving frameworks in cancer biology.
